Intro

Zoloft (Sertraline) is SSRI medication that is used in the treatment of depression, anxiety disorders and panic attacks

It works by blocking the reuptake of serotonin leading to increased serotonin levels in the neurons synapse

It is generally well tolerated by most patients, but sometimes may lead to side effects that will be explained here

Random Side effects

Diarrhea

Nausea and abdominal pain

Dry mouth

Lightheadedness

Yawning

Insomnia

Dizziness

Excessive Sweating

Confusion

Tremor

Fatigue

Weight gain

Emotional blunting

Reduced intensity of positive and negative emotions, apathy and decreased motivation

This is dose dependent

Sexual side effects

Anorgasmia, decreased libido, genital numbness and sexual anhedonia in both genders, erectile dysfunction in males

Mechanism of by which Zoloft causes sexual side effects is not very well understood

Sexual side effects are managed with the use of medications such as sildenafil

Increased Suicide risk

Higher risk of suicide especially during the first few months of the use of this medication especially in people younger than 25 years old

Withdrawal syndrome

Occur where there is abrupt interruptions or sudden withdrawal of the medication

Symptoms include dizziness, insomnia, anxiety, agitation and irritability

This might occur even when missing a single dose

Higher risk for Bipolar switch

This side effect occur in patients with bipolar disorder

Zoloft may precipitate the switch from depression in to hypomania or mania especially when used as monotherapy

the risk of switching is back to normal if Zoloft is taken with mood stabilizers

Increased bleeding risk

Because it may inhibit platelet aggregation

QT interval prolongation

QT interval prolongation: this is dose dependent and not that significant compared with other SSRI (citalopram)

Serotonin syndrome

Caused by increased the serotonin levels

Occurs especially in case of combination of Zoloft with other drugs that elevate the serotonin levels like the TCA, triptans, tramadol, lithium, St John’s wort and tryptophan

Symptoms of serotonin syndrome include altered mental status, autonomic changes such as tachycardia and neuromuscular changes such as tremor, rigidity and myoclonus

Induce SIADH

This occur especially in patients aged 65 and older

Lead to hyponatremia

This lead to symptoms like muscle pain, headache and disorientation
